system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
Sam said that 1/3 of a pie is less than 1/4 of the same pie.

Is Sam correct? ____

Use the circles below to show why this is so.

[Image: Two circles]

Shade in 1/3 of this circle

Shade in 1/4 of this circle

Figure, described in words:
Two identical, empty circles are shown side by side. Below the left circle is the text "Shade in 1/3 of this circle" with 1/3 written as a vertical fraction. Below the right circle is the text "Shade in 1/4 of this circle" with 1/4 written as a vertical fraction.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: No. Drawing description: In the first circle (under 'Shade in 1/3 of this circle'), divide the circle into 3 equal parts and shade 1 of the parts. In the second circle (under 'Shade in 1/4 of this circle'), divide the circle into 4 equal parts by drawing a vertical line and a horizontal line through the center, and shade 1 of the parts. Explanation: The shaded piece for 1/3 is larger than the shaded piece for 1/4, showing that 1/3 of a pie is greater than 1/4 of the same pie, so Sam is not correct.
